# Memory budget fix: software verification

No full-size 64 GB model allocation was performed. The catalogue includes small GPU and synthetic-checkpoint checks; the memory matrix and context policy use simulated hardware. These results do not measure speed on a 64 GB Mac.

Commands: `slotstream-checks --tier t0 --tier t1 --tier t2 --tier t3 --json`; `Tools/static_gates.sh`; `Tools/planner_gates.sh`; `python3 Tools/memory_override_gate.py --binary BINARY --out REPORT`; `Tools/installer_gates.sh`; `python3 Tools/context_gates.py --binary BINARY --report REPORT`; `python3 Tools/context_acceptance.py proxy --out OUTPUT`; `python3 Tools/context_proxy.py --out OUTPUT`. BINARY is the frozen executable identified below.

The first full static invocation stopped at one stale planner assertion. The new busy-start rule selects the base window; the assertion was corrected to require that window and its diagnostic without assuming which larger candidate's refusal is reported first. All planner checks and the remaining memory and installer components then passed. Earlier static components were unchanged and passed in the first invocation.

The broad context acceptance passed before the final MTP-off tier fixture correction. That fixture is a different machine description from the decimal-GB MTP-on tiers. The affected CLI contracts and production source policy were rerun against the final fixture and passed; both final reports are included. The final native check catalogue is bound to the final binary.

      "code": 0,
      "stdout": "OVERVIEW: Measure what reading an N-token prompt costs on this Mac: time,\ntok/s, peak memory, and whether it stayed inside the plan\n\nUSAGE: slotstream context-check <options>\n\nOPTIONS:\n  --model <model>         Model name or directory (default\n                          qwen3.8-flash-next:4bit; a name resolves to the dev\n                          checkout's models/ or ~/.slotstream/models) (default:\n                          qwen3.8-flash-next:4bit)\n  --memory-gb <memory-gb> Total memory target for the whole process, in GB.\n        The easiest knob: how much of this Mac slotstream may use. The expert\n        cache gets what remains after the conservatively charged\n        resident/runtime/context footprint and a 1 GB margin. Run `slotstream\n        doctor --memory-gb N` for the exact cache size. This is a budget, not\n        an instruction to fill RAM: context and temporary workspace use memory\n        as needed. Auto will not trade away cache above the measured decode\n        range for more context; --max-context N chooses that tradeoff\n        explicitly. Default: auto -- a model-specific target based on measured\n        tradeoffs, bounded by 70% of RAM, the Metal working set minus 2 GB, and\n        live availability. The chosen plan is announced at startup. An explicit\n        target pins the cache and disables auto resizing. --experts-per-layer /\n        --pool-gb take precedence.\n  --experts-per-layer <experts-per-layer>\n                          Expert cache size, in experts per layer (1...512).\n        The precise memory<->speed knob. Each of the 48 layers has 512 experts\n        of 2.76 MB; the cache holds N x 48 of them, so pool = N x 0.133 GB\n        (e.g. 226/layer = 30 GB, 181/layer = 24 GB, 30/layer = 4 GB) plus the\n        fixed runtime/context footprint. The pool itself is one GLOBAL cache\n        shared across layers -- N is the intuitive unit, not a per-layer quota:\n        hot layers borrow slots from cold ones. Takes precedence over\n        --memory-gb/--pool-gb. Default: auto (see `slotstream doctor`).\n  --pool-gb <pool-gb>     Raw expert-pool size in GB (1 GB \u2248 7.5\n                          experts/layer). Beats --memory-gb; loses to\n                          --experts-per-layer.\n  --max-ram-percent <max-ram-percent>\n                          Auto only: the largest share of this Mac's RAM auto\n                          may target (default 70).\n        Lower it to keep more of the machine for your other apps; auto still\n        sizes down on its own when they are actually holding memory. It cannot\n        raise the model's default ceiling, which reflects measured tradeoffs on\n        tested hardware. Use --memory-gb for an explicit target beyond that\n        ceiling. Ignored when an explicit memory knob is given.\n  --mtp <mtp>             Speculative decode with the MTP draft head: auto | on\n                          | off (default auto). (default: auto)\n        The model's own next-next-token head drafts 2 tokens by default and the\n        main model verifies them in one batched pass. SLOTSTREAM_DRAFT_DEPTH\n        overrides the depth (1...16). Costs a fixed 1.6 GB of memory; auto\n        enables it only when the expert cache still reaches ~120 experts/layer\n        after paying, which is where the multiplier beats spending the same RAM\n        on cache. Needs the separately converted mtp.safetensors next to the\n        model (Tools/mtp_convert.py).\n  --vision <vision>       Accept images: auto | on | off (default auto).\n                          (default: auto)\n        The checkpoint carries a vision tower; auto loads it the first time a\n        request sends a picture and keeps it resident after that (0.9 GB,\n        reserved inside the process memory target before loading). Image\n        attention also needs workspace. A request is refused if its reservation\n        or real headroom is insufficient. off refuses images outright.\n  --tokens <tokens>       Prompt length in tokens (rungs double from 2048 up to\n                          here with --ladder) (default: 8192)\n  --reply-tokens <reply-tokens>\n                          Required output tokens, reserved before loading\n                          (default: 16)\n  --max-prefill-wait <max-prefill-wait>\n                          Accepted request to first token budget in minutes; 0\n                          disables only time (default: 30.0)\n  --wall-seconds <wall-seconds>\n                          Independent wall-clock ceiling for each diagnostic\n                          rung (default: 7200.0)\n  --sample-footprint      Compatibility flag; context qualification always\n                          samples physical footprint every 20 ms\n  --ladder                Run 2048, 4096, ... up to --tokens, stopping at the\n                          first rung that leaves the plan\n  --plan-only             Print the unqualified plan and exact runtime controls\n                          without loading an Engine\n  --warm-conversations <warm-conversations>\n                          Retain this many distinct conversations and\n                          interleave follow-ups before the capacity request\n                          (0...4) (default: 0)\n  --warm-tokens <warm-tokens>\n                          Prompt tokens in each retained warm-up conversation\n                          (default: 2048)\n  --min-free-gb <min-free-gb>\n                          Abort a pass when reclaimable memory falls below this\n                          (default: the planner's slack, 5% of RAM, at least\n                          1.5 GB)\n  --json                  Machine-readable output, one object per rung\n  --version               Show the version.\n  -h, --help              Show help information.\n\n",
